title: Mars Has Two Speeds of Sound, So High Notes Arrive First

scenes.text: On Mars, high notes reach your ear before low ones.
NASA's Perseverance rover carried microphones. Mars was so quiet the team thought one was broken.
Then they timed the crack of its laser zapping rocks: about 250 meters a second.
But the low hum of the Ingenuity helicopter traveled only about 240.
The thin carbon dioxide air slows low pitches more than high ones.
On Earth, both arrive together at 343 meters a second. On Mars, a song would reach you out of order.

description:
Perseverance's microphones showed that on Mars, high-pitched sounds travel at about 250 meters per second while low-pitched sounds travel at about 240 (Nature, 2022).
The team measured the laser's sparks and the Ingenuity helicopter's hum. On Earth sound travels at about 343 meters per second, and on Mars it fades within about 8 meters versus about 65 on Earth.
What would you want to hear first on Mars?
first_comment: Sound also dies out after about 8 meters on Mars. Would you even hear someone shouting across the street?
